direction.name: The sentence is the layout
direction.idea: One short sentence, set at poster scale, is the composition. The trick that makes it an idea rather than a big headline: something from the subject sits inside the sentence where a word would be. A strip of photograph fills the gap between two words; a small live fragment of the product replaces the noun; the object the sentence names is pictured at the size of a letter. Write the sentence first, find the word that can be shown instead of said, and put the showing in its place. The reader completes the sentence with their eyes.
direction.composition: The sentence is four to seven words and runs as one or two full-width lines at 9–13vw. Inline with the type, on the baseline, sits one media slot: a rounded-rectangle or square frame exactly one line-height tall and two to three ems wide, holding a photograph or a looping crop. Above and below the sentence the screen is empty except for a small navigation line and one supporting sentence set small, both on the same left margin. Later sections repeat the grammar at smaller scale: each is a short statement on the left six columns with its proof (image, figure, list) on the right, so the page reads as a series of sentences with evidence. Generous vertical space (160px or more) between sections.
direction.typography: Display weight with real presence (medium to bold), tracking -0.03 to -0.05em, leading 0.95–1.0 so two lines sit close. The inline frame aligns to cap height and baseline exactly; set it with em units so it scales with the type.
direction.colour: A calm ground with ink at full contrast. The only colour comes from the photograph inside the sentence; if the palette has an accent, use it once, on the action.
direction.imagery: One strong, simple photograph that reads at small size (a face, an object, a texture, a horizon), cropped to a wide strip inside the sentence. The same image may open to full width in the next section, so the small slot feels like a window onto something larger.
direction.richness: The collision of big type and one live image inside it. Because there is only one image on the first screen, choose it with care and give it perfect alignment to the letters.
direction.pitfalls: The sentence must be short enough for two lines on a phone, where the inline frame drops to its own line between the two halves. Do not style one word differently to fake the device. Do not use more than one slot per sentence.

hero.name: Sentence with a photo strip
hero.blueprint: A warm flat ground with no navigation bar. One sentence of four or five words runs as a single line of condensed capitals at clamp(120px, 13vw, 200px), sitting on the vertical centre and reaching edge to edge inside 28px margins. Where one word of the sentence would be, a strip of photograph takes its place: a frame exactly one cap-height tall (set in em) and 45–50% of the viewport wide, ratio near 5:1, corners radiused 14px, `object-fit: cover`. Build the line as a flex row with `align-items: baseline` and give the strip `flex: 1` so words and picture always fill the width. The photograph shows the thing the sentence names: a wide view of the place, taken from above or along a horizon, so it survives the letterbox crop. The top third of the screen is empty apart from a 15px wordmark top-left and two text links top-right. About 150px under the sentence the single action sits centred as a small solid button. One supporting sentence at 22px, max 44ch, is centred 48px above the bottom edge.
hero.mobile: The sentence breaks into two lines at 21vw with the strip between them: the first words, then the photograph as a 2:1 frame at full width minus 16px margins with the same 14px corners, then the remaining words. The block is centred vertically. The action button sits 32px under the last line and the supporting sentence under that at 16px. The top links collapse to one word.
hero.headline: A sentence of four or five short words, about 14 characters of type in total, whose missing word is the photograph.

type.note: An American gothic for headings over a sober transitional serif for reading, the pairing of a newspaper front page. Suits essays, annual reports, archives and finance pages that have real paragraphs.

palette.name: Stone and blueprint
palette.note: Stone paper carries the whole page with near-black and grey text. One image at a time is printed in the accent blue as its only ink, and the same blue fills the single button.

motion.name: Shutter image
motion.description: The one hero or showcase image opens from an edge with a clip-path over about 1.1 seconds while the picture inside settles from 1.12 scale to rest. Use it once, on the image that matters most; later images simply are there. Recipe: 'Image shutter' in references/motion.md.

sections.name: Headline crossing onto a photograph
sections.blueprint: A white or pale ground. A photograph taller than it is wide, 720px wide (columns 7–12), sits flush against the right viewport edge with its top at 46% of the section's first screen and runs below the fold. The heading starts on the 32px left margin across columns 1–8: two lines of light-weight serif capitals at clamp(64px, 5.6vw, 88px), leading 1.04, the first line starting 34% down the screen and the second placed so that its right half runs onto the photograph's upper-left corner. Choose a picture whose upper-left quarter is pale enough for the ink, or set the second line twice, in the ink and in the paper colour, each copy clipped to its side of the photograph's left edge. Under the heading on columns 1–5, one paragraph of up to 25 words at 22px, leading 1.4. At the bottom-left a second, smaller photograph of 360×400px enters, cropped by the screen's lower edge, and on the next screen becomes the left half of a staggered pair with the large one. Nothing else is on the screen.
sections.mobile: The heading sits at 10vw on two lines on the 20px margin. The photograph becomes 75% of the width, flush right, and starts under the heading's first line so the second line crosses its top-left corner. The paragraph follows at 17px, then the small photograph at 50% of the width on the left margin.

sections.name: Prints dropped on the headline
sections.blueprint: A flat colour field 100svh tall. A two-line headline of two to four words in an ultra-condensed or ultra-heavy face is centred, each line clamp(120px, 14vw, 210px) tall with leading 0.85. Two portrait photographs, each about 26vw wide at 3:4 with an 8px solid white border like a print, are absolutely placed on top of the headline's centre: one rotated −8 degrees, one +6 degrees, overlapping each other by a third and hiding roughly half the letters, so the eye completes the words. A third, smaller print (16vw) may sit at the lower right, cropped by the section's bottom edge. One plain sentence at 16px sits at the bottom-left margin, 24px from the edges. The prints are above the type in the stacking order; hovering one brings it to the front and straightens it to 0 degrees over 200ms. Nothing else is on the field.
sections.mobile: Headline lines at 30vw, still two lines, centred in a 78svh field. Two prints only, each 52vw wide, rotated −6 and +5 degrees, overlapping at the headline's centre. The small sentence sits at the bottom-left margin at 15px.

sections.name: Statement, table pushed right
sections.blueprint: A heading of four to six words spans the full width on two lines at clamp(40px, 4.5vw, 68px), left-aligned with its first line indented 3vw and leading 0.98. 96px below, the table is pushed into the right-hand five columns (8–12) and the left stays open. One plain word naming the table (offices, hours, rates) hangs at 14px in column 7, top-aligned with the first row. Each row is a three-part line at 15–16px with 26px between rows: the kind or day in the soft ink at the left of the measure, the place or service at 30%, and the address, time or price right-aligned, with a small arrow where the row links. Rows are separated by space only; every fourth row has 44px above it to form groups. In columns 1–4, bottom-aligned with the last row, one 4:5 photograph 22vw wide may sit alone. Holds 5–14 rows.
sections.mobile: Heading at 9.5vw without the indent. The table takes the full width at 16px; each row stacks the kind above the place, with the value right-aligned on the first line. The naming word is dropped because the heading already says it. The photograph follows at 60% width on the right margin.

sections.name: Portrait as drop cap
sections.blueprint: No heading. One biography paragraph of 50–80 words is set large at clamp(24px, 2.5vw, 38px), regular weight, leading 1.2, across columns 3–12 of the grid. A square portrait is floated at the paragraph's start with `float: left`: its side equals three lines of text (3.6em), with 0.5em of space to its right, so the first three lines wrap beside it and the fourth returns to the paragraph's left edge, like a drop capital. Square corners. The person's name, the first words of the paragraph, is in full ink; the rest may be in a softer ink with linked names in full ink and underlined. A second paragraph follows after one blank line in the soft ink at the same size. Columns 1–2 hold three short facts (place, since when, how to reach) at 14px, top-aligned with the portrait. Section padding 140px.
sections.mobile: Text at 22px with leading 1.25, full width. The portrait keeps its float but grows to four lines tall, about 110px square. The three facts move below the second paragraph as a single row of three small blocks at 13px.

sections.name: Question at both edges
sections.blueprint: For a closing choice between two answers: book or ask, this date or that, the tasting or the tour. A flat field exactly 100svh tall in the darkest tone. The question is a two-line heading at clamp(110px, 11vw, 168px), leading 1.0, centred, about 54% of the width: line one with its cap line 32px under the field's top edge, line two with its baseline 24px above the bottom edge. The band of about 560px between them is empty except for one row at its optical centre: two solid rectangular buttons, each about 200×56px with its label at 18px in medium weight, their inner edges 120px either side of the centre axis, and between them, exactly on the axis, the word 'or' at 18px in the soft ink. 16px under the row, centred, one line at 16px in the soft ink says what happens after either choice. The type above and below closes the empty band, so it reads as held breath rather than a gap.
sections.mobile: The question drops to 18vw, still two centred lines, line one 32px from the top and line two 24px above the bottom. The buttons stack at the centre at 72% of the width, 12px apart, with 'or' between them and the line of explanation under the second.

sections.name: Contact as the headline
sections.blueprint: A full-bleed field in one saturated palette colour, at least 90svh tall. Top row, 40px from the edge: two or three short notes at 15px in columns 1–7 (address, hours, a one-line description) and a back-to-top text link at the right margin. Then a tall empty gap. In the lower half, the way to get in touch is the display line: the telephone number or the email address itself, set at 8–9vw, flush left, hard against the margin, as one link. An email address may break once, before the @, giving two lines. Size it with `clamp()` so the longest line fills at least 80% of the width. Under it, one row of small text at 14px spread across three positions: links at the left, credits in the centre, city and year at the right. The wordmark appears only small, in the top row.
sections.mobile: Notes stack at the top at 15px. The contact line sits in the lower half at 12vw; a telephone number stays on one line, an email breaks before the @ and is sized so each half fits the width. The meta row becomes three stacked lines at 13px.

references.name: Spatial
references.idea: Typography behaves like sound in a room: plain black statements swell, stretch and bend through an empty white viewport as you scroll.
references.hero: A white viewport holding only the festival dates: two centred lines in Neue Haas Grotesk Roman at roughly 6.7vw, black, tight leading, sitting at the exact vertical middle and spanning about half the width. Large empty fields above and below; no image, no button, no supporting copy. The header is the only other element: a light uppercase wordmark with tight tracking flush to the top-left corner at a 20px inset, and nine small bold uppercase links in a row across the top right. Mobile is the same poster at 40px with a two-line hamburger.
references.type: One face, Neue Haas Grotesk Display 55 Roman, for everything: statements from 56px up to about 10vw, 13px body, bold 13px uppercase navigation, a timetable at about 16px with tight leading. Statement lines are distorted per glyph, each letter scaled to a different width and height.
references.colour: #ffffff #000000 #e8a25c — Pure black on pure white; the programme section inverts to white on black. The only colour is the amber haze of a single photograph.
references.imagery: Almost none. The images are canvas-rendered text statements warped and magnified until letter fragments become abstract black shapes cropped by the viewport. One warm, hazy venue photograph sits inset at half width beside body copy, square-cornered.
references.layout: Full width with 10 to 20px margins. Opens with one centred statement per screen, then drops into left-aligned two-column copy and, further down, edge-to-edge four-column timetables. The swing between empty poster screens and tightly packed listings is the page's rhythm.

sections.description: A run of full-viewport white screens, each carrying one centred two-line sentence. The text is drawn on canvas and deformed: letters within a word have different widths and heights and baselines wobble. Between screens the type is magnified so far that only the strokes and counters of a few letters cross the frame, cropped on every side, while a small readable version of the next sentence appears inside the wreckage of the previous one.

A calm reset: a three-line centred statement at about 5vw in undistorted type fills the top half. At the bottom, a column of 16px body copy about 650px wide sits flush to the left margin, and an amber-toned photograph starts at the horizontal centre and runs to the right margin with square corners, cropped by the fold.

Black full-bleed section. Day headings are single small lines above a hairline; under each, a four-column table spans the full width: artist flush left, format at one third, room at two thirds, time range right-aligned at the far edge. Rows are about 35px high with a hairline between each, all in the same 30px grotesk with no bold; changeovers are marked by rows in capitals.

steal: Open with a single factual line (the dates) centred on an otherwise empty white screen instead of a branded hero.
Scale each letter of a statement independently in width and height so plain grotesk type looks as if it is resonating.
Set a programme as a full-width four-column hairline table in one size and weight, times right-aligned, on an inverted background.

references.name: bleibtgleich’26
references.idea: One thin vertical rule runs down the page and a tight bold grotesk sentence wraps around it, words stepping from one side of the line to the other.
references.hero: White page, black type. Content sits in a narrow band between 26% and 68% of the width. A 1px vertical rule drops from the top edge at 37% for two-thirds of the height. Left of it: a black blob avatar at the top, a tiny role caption at its foot. Right of it: a tiny location note at the top, the name in two lines of 90px medium grotesk at the bottom. The tagline continues below at the same size, flush to the band's left edge, running past the fold. The upper half is otherwise blank. The handle is split into two pale-grey words fixed in the bottom corners; a black menu pill sits top-right.
references.type: Akzidenz Grotesk Pro medium only, -0.05em tracking, line-height about 0.9. Two sizes: 90px (6.3vw) for every statement and 11-13px for captions and table rows, a 7:1 jump. Long words are hyphenated and stepped across lines on purpose.
references.colour: #ffffff #000000 #e4e4e4 #f2f2f2 — Black on white with no accent. Pale grey is used for the ghosted corner wordmark and a few small square tiles; tiny coloured rings inside those tiles are the only hue.
references.imagery: Almost none: a black blob avatar, a few 85px grey tiles each with a coloured ring, and a canvas dome of small tilted project thumbnails floating between two words.
references.layout: Everything hangs off one vertical axis at 37%: lines start either at the axis or one indent to its left, giving a stepped rag. Very wide white margins. Sections are separated by a full screen of white rather than rules or colour.

sections.description: A 90px sentence is typeset word by word around the vertical rule: one word ends just left of the rule, the next starts just right of it, and the following line is centred beneath both. Above the sentence a row of five 85px pale-grey squares, each with a small coloured ring at its centre, is spaced unevenly along one baseline, with a three-line 13px description under the second.

The heading first appears as one centred line near the bottom of an empty screen, then its two halves separate to the far left and far right edges at mid-height. In the gap a WebGL dome of fifteen or so small project thumbnails, mostly black and white, tilts in perspective like tiles on a sphere. Nothing else is on the screen.

The heading is broken into an ampersand alone in the left margin and two words stepped over three lines with a hyphen break and a growing indent. Below it a four-column table at 11px: year, site name, awarding body, award. Hairline rules sit under every row, columns align to the hero's band, and year groups are separated by a blank row.

The closing sentence is stepped over four lines with shifting indents, right of centre. To its left two tiny grey captions and an email address at 11px. Under it three 36px outlined circles with social initials, centred, then the handle at about 44px centred on the bottom edge with tiny legal text in the two corners.

steal: Draw one 1px vertical rule and typeset a large sentence around it, alternating words to either side so the line becomes the text's spine.
Split the logotype into two words, ghost them at about 10% grey, and fix one in each bottom corner of the viewport.
Leave the top half of the hero blank and start the name at 50% height so the headline runs off the fold and pulls the scroll.
references.media: No picture on the first screen, which is all type plus a small black mark. Pictures arrive later as a WebGL sphere of project thumbnails flanked by two words that slide apart on scroll, square tiles placed on separate grid cells with empty cells between them, hover thumbnails behind a text index, and one small image used as a glyph in a row of numerals; no video.
references.motion: A 2.5s progress counter runs although the page loaded in 1.5s, while a vertical line draws down with the role label at its tip. Lenis and 15 ScrollTriggers with nothing pinned: display lines rise by yPercent over 0.47s in-out at a 0.075s stagger, the globe's rotation is scrubbed across its 1178px block, the flanking words are pulled apart on a scrub, and underlines wipe in by background-size over 0.6s cubic-bezier(0.76,0,0.24,1).

references.name: Mosby’s Files
references.idea: An archive of architects presented as a physical stack of coloured index-tab file folders that you flip through.
references.hero: Charcoal background. A slim top bar over a hairline holds the condensed wordmark dead centre and one mono link far right. The headline is one centred line of heavy condensed uppercase at 10vw, about 71% of the width, in the upper quarter. Beneath it, a three-line centred serif paragraph in mid-grey, about 42% wide. From 51% down sits a stack of file folders 86% of the viewport wide: each is a flat colour band with one to three trapezoid tabs rising from its top-left edge, each tab a different colour holding a serif name. Mono category labels sit right-aligned. The front red folder is open, running off the bottom.
references.type: Founders Grotesk bold condensed uppercase at 144px for the title and wordmark; Signifier serif at about 22px for the intro and 28px for tab names; IBM Plex Mono 12px for labels and body. Three unrelated faces, each with one job, and a twelve-to-one size jump.
references.colour: #191919 #d71e1e #1e4bd7 #0c7866 #581e70 #ffe927 — Charcoal ground with five flat poster primaries assigned to folders and tabs; each tab deliberately differs from the folder behind it. No tints, gradients or photos; white type except black on yellow.
references.imagery: No photographs on the index. The folder shapes are the imagery, plus a row of seven small white line-drawn north-arrow and compass symbols and a drawing scale bar borrowed from architectural plans.
references.layout: Centred title block over an 86%-wide folder stack with equal dark margins. Folders overlap at a fixed 60px step so only the tab rows show; the open folder expands into a tall single-colour panel with mono text top-left and plan symbols near the bottom. Under two screens.

sections.description: Four full-width colour bands stacked with a 60px reveal, each with trapezoid tabs growing from its top-left edge. Tabs are about 44px tall with S-curved shoulders, sit side by side with small gaps, and each takes a contrasting flat colour: yellow and black tabs on a green folder, red and blue on purple. Names are white serif at 28px inside the tabs. A mono category label with a small chevron is right-aligned in each band's visible strip.

The front folder opens into a solid red panel nearly two viewports tall. Top-right: its mono category label with a down chevron. Top-left, inset about 60px: a four-line mono paragraph in white, at most half the panel wide. The middle is left empty. Near the bottom, a centred row of seven small white plan symbols evenly spaced; beneath, a baseline row with a drawing scale bar left, year centre, credit and round logo right.

steal: Build navigation as stacked full-width colour bands with trapezoid tabs, each tab coloured to clash with the folder behind it.
Pair a heavy condensed grotesk title with a bookish serif for names and a mono for metadata, giving each face exactly one role.
Borrow notation from the subject's own documents (scale bars, north arrows) as footer ornament instead of generic icons.
references.media: The hero has no picture: its visual weight is a CSS stack of overlapping flat colour folders with sloped tabs covering the lower half of the fold (about 42% of the area), which doubles as the index; an open folder expands to 80vh as the content panel. The only drawings are seven small white plan symbols and a scale bar; no photographs or video on the index.
references.motion: A short entrance: readable at about 1.2s, with 17 title letter spans already in place, and settled by 2.5s as the stack rises about 13px into place and the subline fades up. Lenis on a page only 1.6 screens tall; the header slides away on scroll, and folders and tabs move on one house curve, cubic-bezier(.33,1,.68,1), at 0.65s, with the quicker moves at exactly half that, 0.325s.
